content.value_statement: Machine learning teams need clear reasons for model predictions and feature influence. This skill provides SHAP workflows, explainer selection, plots, and interpretation guidance for common model types.
actual_capabilities: Selects an appropriate SHAP explainer for tree, deep learning, linear, and black-box models.
Shows how to compute SHAP values and interpret base values, feature contributions, and output units.
Guides global and local visualizations, including beeswarm, bar, waterfall, scatter, force, and heatmap plots.
Provides workflows for model debugging, feature engineering, model comparison, fairness analysis, and production use.
Explains performance strategies such as sampling, batching, cached explainers, and top-feature limits.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run model training or compute explanations by itself.
Users must supply their own model, data, feature names, and target interpretation question.
SHAP explanations show model behavior and association, not causal proof.
Large datasets or model-agnostic explainers can be slow without sampling or batching.

use_cases.title: Explain a Production Prediction
use_cases.description: Create local SHAP explanations that show which features moved one prediction away from the baseline.

use_cases.title: Audit Feature Importance
use_cases.description: Use global plots and cohort comparisons to find dominant features, leakage signals, or unexpected model behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Fairness Signals
use_cases.description: Compare SHAP values across groups and inspect protected attributes or proxy features during model review.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a SHAP Explainer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known model family.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a [model type] model and a tabular dataset. Help me choose the right SHAP explainer and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Create Core Plots
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate standard global and local interpretation views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through computing SHAP values for my trained model and choosing beeswarm, bar, waterfall, and scatter plots.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Model Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate errors, leakage, or confusing predictions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use SHAP to debug misclassified samples, inspect suspicious feature importance, and validate feature relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Explanation Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced deployment planning for prediction explanations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production SHAP workflow with cached explainers, batched computation, top-feature output, monitoring, and versioning.

output_examples.input: A data scientist asks why a fraud model flagged one transaction.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a local waterfall plot, explains the baseline prediction, and ranks the features that increased or reduced risk.

output_examples.input: A team sees an unexpected feature at the top of global importance.
output_examples.output: The response outlines checks for leakage, cohort differences, feature correlations, and scatter plots for relationship validation.

output_examples.input: An engineer wants SHAP explanations in an API.
output_examples.output: The response proposes saved models and explainers, batched explanation calls, cached results, top-feature summaries, and latency monitoring.

best_practices: Choose specialized explainers before model-agnostic explainers when the model type is known.
Start with global plots, then inspect individual predictions and key feature relationships.
Validate SHAP patterns with domain knowledge and check output units before drawing conclusions.
anti_patterns: Using KernelExplainer for tree models when TreeExplainer is available.
Treating SHAP values as causal evidence without additional analysis.
Explaining huge datasets without sampling, batching, or limiting visual complexity.

faq.question: What models does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers tree models, deep learning models, linear models, and black-box models through the appropriate SHAP explainer.

faq.question: Can it create SHAP plots?
faq.answer: It guides plot selection and implementation for beeswarm, bar, waterfall, scatter, force, heatmap, violin, and decision plots.

faq.question: Does it compute explanations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples. The user must run the code with their own model and data.

faq.question: Can it help with fairness analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for comparing groups, checking protected attributes, and identifying possible proxy features.

faq.question: How should users handle slow SHAP computations?
faq.answer: Use specialized explainers, representative samples, batching, cached explainers, and top-feature limits for large workloads.

faq.question: Does SHAP prove causation?
faq.answer: No. SHAP explains model behavior and feature association. Causal claims require separate causal analysis.
